newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan wants China medallists to visit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan wants China medallists to visit.

text.p: Taiwan said on Thursday it was inviting Olympic gold medallists from China to visit the island despite a 19-month-long political impasse between Taipei and Beijing.
"We are arranging visits by mainland gold medallists, but details have not been finalised," a spokeswoman at Taiwan's Chinese Taipei Olympic Committee said.
"We are not sure who will come at this moment, but we only invite the very best people," the spokeswoman said.

She declined to confirm a local newspaper report that the mainland Olympic delegation would arrive on February 20, but said the visit might take place after the Lunar New Year, which falls on February 7.
Wu Shaozu, president of Beijing's Chinese Olympic Committee, would head the delegation, the paper said.
China and Taiwan have been rivals since the two split after a civil war in 1949.
Nationalist-ruled Taiwan has banned direct contacts with China's communist government but has allowed a range of unofficial exchanges in the interest of better ties.
Numerous mainland officials were able to visit Taiwan in 1996 under such informal exchanges despite military tensions across the Taiwan Strait.
Beijing suspended semi-official talks with Taiwan and rattled the island with war games after President Lee Teng-hui made a private visit to the United States in mid-1995.
China regarded Lee's U.S. trip as a move towards Taiwan independence.
